units.claim: Domain holds models and use-case interfaces, the innermost entities layer.
Application holds use cases, ports, errors and validations.
Presentation holds controllers, middlewares and response classes.

citations.quote: I'm using the name **"Presentation"** for this layer.

units.claim: Infrastructure holds express, knex and repository implementations (frameworks and drivers).

citations.quote: This folder (layer) is where we add everything related to external "**Frameworks and Drivers**". Here you can add the repositories, external frameworks, web and so on.

units.claim: Main is the composition root with factories that wire everything; it may depend on all layers. The common folder is cross-cutting and belongs to no layer.

citations.quote: This layer is where we put everything together. It's the "dirty layer", because most factories will be here. It may depend on all other layers in the system.

units.claim: Dependencies point inward: main, then infrastructure, then presentation, then application, then domain.

citations.quote: The overriding rule that makes this architecture work is The Dependency Rule. This rule says that source code dependencies can only point inwards.
In our case, data enter the system via "express routes" (infrastructure layer) to the "controllers" (adapters layer), to the "use cases" (application layer), to the "domain" (domain/entities layer).
